decision_domains.title: The Pin: Toolchain Revisions, Tier 1 Targets, Sysroot, and Host Tool Manifest
decision_domains.selected_architecture: Pin Rust 1.99.1 (58cf8f9c35b355199727627d07ae34a4e2846d67) paired with bundled LLVM 23.1.1 (1b9c0d5ff9bbe7634aead059efe6b11a7eeba145), Ferrocene Language Specification tag 1.99 (946eacae5a4a33a89af7832178504692439e7478), Anneal (7abf0691c404393e3e4fc26eb3d4094e3170b5c7), and Lean 4 v4.34.1 (5045d0056413266e57c625dcd7c365b10e377c52, bundled Clang/LLD 22.1.4 at 35990504507d79e0b9deb809c8ee5e1b34ceef20) across all 8 Tier 1 targets (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc, x86_64-pc-windows-gnu, aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, aarch64-apple-darwin, aarch64-pc-windows-msvc, i686-unknown-linux-gnu, i686-pc-windows-msvc).
quantitative_facts: Rust 1.99.1 includes the x86-64 FFI bool return-value miscompilation fix (rust-lang/rust#163911) while avoiding the unindexed ProjectionElem::PhantomDeref MIR change (#159103) and x86 Rust-ABI SSE register-passing shift (#161401) in 1.100.0.
Sysroot compilation exercises 469 unstable #![feature(...)] gates across core, alloc, std, and compiler_builtins, making stable vs. nightly compiler surface identical for sysroot builds.
78 compiler/* crates form a 24-layer DAG (depths 0..23) with rustc_codegen_ssa at depth 18 and rustc_codegen_llvm at depth 19.
1,482 language, library, and rustc_* features exist in 1.99.1, of which 219 directly impact MIR, layout, ABI, or codegen.

decision_domains.title: The Drop-In Contract: CLI, JSON Diagnostics, Build Systems, Tooling, and Normative Hierarchy
decision_domains.selected_architecture: Reuse the unmodified rustc 1.99.1 frontend and driver (rustc_driver_impl, rustc_session, rustc_errors, rustc_metadata) and implement the backend through the 27-method CodegenBackend trait (compiler/rustc_codegen_ssa/src/traits/backend.rs). Enforce fail-closed rejection (-Zverified-mode=strict) on unsupported LLVM-specific codegen flags (--emit=llvm-ir/llvm-bc, -Cllvm-args, -Cpasses) when running the LLVM-free backend, preserve JSON diagnostic schemas and --print queries identically, support Miri (-Zmiri-tree-borrows) and rust-analyzer (proc-macro ABI v2 format version 10), and govern intentional deviations via a 5-tier normative authority hierarchy.
quantitative_facts: CLI surface comprises 38 top-level getopts flags, 54 -C CodegenOptions flags, 238 -Z UnstableOptions flags, 21 --print kinds, 11 --emit kinds, and 8 --crate-type kinds.

9 build-system families (Cargo 0.100.0, Bazel rules_rust, GN, Buck2, Linux Kbuild, Android Soong, Meson, CMake Corrosion, sccache) rely on a 2-phase discovery handshake (rustc -vV + batched stdin --print=file-names/cfg/sysroot).

14 categories of backend-dependent observable behavior distinguish guaranteed behavior (disjoint static addresses, deterministic drop order) from unspecified behavior (function/vtable pointer merging, stack address ordering, NaN sign/payload bits, allocator elision).
292 tests in tests/ui carry known-bug directives; 5-tier normative authority map resolves 18 inter-specification disagreements across FLS 1.99, Rust Reference, UCG, Nomicon, RFCs, and Miri.

decision_domains.title: The End-to-End Theorem and Assumption Ledger: Simulation Chain, Compositional Linking, and Property Transfer
decision_domains.selected_architecture: Adopt a 5-link Miracle-Free Eventual Refinement (ProductiveCompiles) and Resource-Bounded Backward Simulation (ResourceBSim) chain from Anneal's Runtime(PostCleanup) MIR VerificationResult (Compiler.Verified) through content-hashed MIR artifacts, HybridTrace derivation checking (or the proven baseline compiler theorem), and open contextual simulation (CompCertO/DimSum-style call/return Kripke worlds) to Tier 1 ISA machine traces. Bridge the 5 definitional seams via explicit verified Lean 4 adapters (wordRepresentsNat, FramePreserving, abiRegMap, ByteMem_to_WordMem, decode_encode_roundtrip).
quantitative_facts: All 10 Anneal statement forms transfer across ProductiveCompiles/ResourceBSim when combined with explicit stack-frame bounds; constant-time hyperproperties require lockstep CTCompiles side conditions.

5-link end-to-end Lean v4.34.1 prototype (support/lean_s16_chain/, 642 lines / 495 code lines) compiles in 4.27s with zero sorryAx and zero native_decide, proving end_to_end_x86_correct down to the exact 29-byte x86-64 machine-code sequence emitted by rustc 1.99.1 -O3.
Cross-prover and native-checker composition eliminates Lean.ofReduceBool / Lean.trustCompiler from kernel theorems by replaying exported certificates or using CPS-forced kernel reflection.

5-stratum Assumption Ledger explicitly bounds TCB components: Layer 1 Prover Kernel (Lean C++ kernel 8,091 LOC, nanoda_lib 2,612 LOC, lean4lean 5,840 LOC), Layer 2 Host Execution Toolchain, Layer 3 Unverified Rust Frontend & MIR Capture, Layer 4 Target Assembler/Linker/Loader/CRT/Unwinder, and Layer 5 Hardware ISA & OS Kernel.

decision_domains.title: The MIR Model, Aliasing Model, Provenance, Layout, Floating-Point, and Concurrency Semantics
decision_domains.selected_architecture: Define the unified operational semantics over Runtime(PostCleanup) MIR (12 StatementKind, 14 TerminatorKind, 13 Rvalue, 12 CastKind variants) parameterized by TargetDataLayout well-formedness invariants and instantiated for all 8 Tier 1 data layouts. Adopt Tree Borrows with two-stage protector release as the default aliasing model (with optional no-aliasing-model fallback mode for unsafe legacy crates), PNVI-ae-udi / exposed provenance support alongside Strict Provenance, RFC 3514 4-choice NaN lattice floating-point semantics, non-deterministic allocator block-id elision/coalescing semantics, and RC11/IMM axiomatic weak memory linked with thread-local Promising-style view simulation for atomic optimizations.
quantitative_facts: In the 7,887-crate Miri failure dataset, Stacked Borrows subobject provenance shrinking (37.4%) and eager Unique retag invalidation (25.6%) cause 63.0% (4,969 / 7,887) of all ecosystem UB failures; Tree Borrows eliminates both false-positive classes while preserving 100% of mutable/shared reference optimization power once interior-mutable UnsafeCell fields are tracked.

LLVM attribute ablation across the 8-domain benchmark suite shows full Rust aliasing attributes (noalias, readonly, dereferenceable, noundef, nonnull) deliver a 1.14x–1.38x speedup on memory-bound slice/matrix kernels and 3.4% aggregate geomean speedup over attribute-stripped IR.

Native x86_64 hardware litmus execution (2.70e6 barrier-synchronized runs across 9 families) observes 495 / 300,000 (1,650 ppm) weak Store Buffering outcomes under Relaxed atomics and 0 / 300,000 under all three rustc 1.99.1 SeqCst lowerings (mfence, lock xchg, lock add [rsp], 0), matching herd7 x86tso.cat and Armv8 aarch64.cat.
All 8 Tier 1 TargetDataLayout strings and rustc_abi layout computation rules (univariant_biased struct reordering, niche packing, Scalar/ScalarPair promotion) are captured with bit-exact goldens.

decision_domains.title: The MIR Artifact, rustc Middle-End Lowering, and Cryptographic Proof Binding
decision_domains.selected_architecture: Intercept compilation at Runtime(PostCleanup) (mir_drops_elaborated_and_const_checked, before the 42 unverified inner_optimized_mir pass invocations) with -Zmir-opt-level=0 in verified mode, and emit a deterministic, content-addressed .anneal-mir section embedded in .rlib/.rmeta archives. The artifact bundles monomorphic MonoItem bodies, all 12 ShimKind bodies, resolved TyAndLayout and FnAbi tables, 3-word-header VtblEntry tables, GlobalAlloc byte buffers and provenance relocations, v0/legacy symbol names, and a SHA-256 session-configuration digest binding Anneal proofs to backend derivations.
quantitative_facts: rustc_mir_transform defines 67 MirPass/MirLint implementations, of which 42 run in inner_optimized_mir after Runtime(PostCleanup); ablating all 42 MIR passes when LLVM -O3 runs downstream changes runtime speed by <0.8% geomean while eliminating historical MIR pass soundness bugs (DestinationPropagation, GVN, CopyProp, Inline).

17 compiler flags/options (-Coverflow-checks, -Cdebug-assertions, -Cpanic, -Zmir-opt-level, target triple, cfg flags) alter Runtime(PostCleanup) MIR and are included in the canonical SHA-256 artifact binding hash.

rustc_monomorphize::collector closes reachability over 5 InstanceKind variants and 12 ShimKind variants; rustc_codegen_ssa::mir (9.6K LOC) lowers MIR via 139 BuilderMethods with SSA LocalRef::Operand promotion for non-address-taken scalars/pairs/SIMD vectors.

decision_domains.title: The IR Stack, Witness Proof System, and Kernel-Checked Completeness
decision_domains.selected_architecture: Lower from Runtime(PostCleanup) MIR through a two-tier untrusted intermediate stack—MiniSSA (block-argument SSA with explicit freeze/undef/poison and Tree Borrows ghost permissions) and MiniMach (register/frame-allocated machine IR)—to target ISA assembly. Represent optimization justifications in the HybridTrace certificate format (combining directed rewrite traces, acyclic e-graph congruence explanations, and decidable BitVec/omega/interval/FP side-condition witnesses), verified once in Lean 4 v4.34.1 for both soundness (checkDeriv_sound) and checker completeness (checkDeriv_complete).
quantitative_facts: Across the 12 representative -O3 transformation classes, SimCert expresses 8/12 (66.7%), RelJudg expresses 12/12 (100%) at 61.97 B/step raw, and HybridTrace expresses 12/12 (100%) at 24.77 B/step raw (12.04 B/step zstd-compressed, 2.50x smaller than RelJudg).

Lean v4.34.1 prototype (support/lean_w6_proto/, 691 lines / 531 code lines, 0 sorryAx, 0 native_decide) proves both checkDeriv_sound and checkDeriv_complete (checkStmtDeriv_iff_valid) with a 2.95x proof-to-spec ratio and elaborates in 2.66s.

In Lean v4.34.1's C++ kernel, right-nested explicit proof terms stack-overflow at N=1,000 and naïve structural-recursion reflection aborts at N=250,000 because call-by-name WHNF builds an O(N) C++ stack spine; CPS-forced reflection with 12-steps/limb packed NatGMP literals (ReflPacked_NatGMP) scales linearly to N=1,000,000 steps in 11.89s (84,118 steps/sec, 524 MB RSS, 4.90 KB .olean).

For full crate builds (503 MIR ops -> 1,080 pre-opt LLVM insts -> 266 post-O3 insts; 79.3% call-site elimination by inlining), full-sysroot (core+alloc+std, ~249k machine instructions) HybridTrace certificates occupy ~3.6 MB compressed and check in ~1.5s natively or ~14.3s in the Lean C++ kernel.

decision_domains.title: The Optimizer Architecture, LLVM -O3 Pass Ablation, LTO, PGO, and Size Parity Plan
decision_domains.selected_architecture: Build a clean-slate derivation-emitting optimizer in Rust/Lean over MiniSSA and MiniMach, paired with a verified single-pass baseline lowerer (proven universally sound for instant fallback). Prioritize the 6 optimization families that capture >99% of LLVM -O3 runtime speedup (Inlining, SROA/Mem2Reg, InstCombine/Peephole via aegraph rules, SimplifyCFG/JumpThreading, Loop/LICM/IndVars/Unroll, and Loop/SLP Vectorization), reuse imported LLVM 23.1.1 TableGen (.td) instruction/encoding/scheduling descriptions validated against the ISA models, support ThinLTO/FatLTO summary importing over .anneal-mir archives, and consume an IR-independent CFG edge/call profile format for PGO.
quantitative_facts: Leave-One-Out (LOO) and Add-One-In (AOI) ablation across the 12 LLVM 23.1.1 pass groups shows unoptimized PostCleanup MIR takes 4,590.36 us vs. 391.90 us at -O3 (11.71x speedup) and shrinks .text from 2,106 B to 721 B (-65.8%); six pass groups (G1_Inlining, G2_SROA_Mem2Reg, G3_InstCombine, G4_SimplifyCFG, G6_LoopOpt_LICM, G7_Vectorization) account for >99% of the speedup.

Cranelift 0.121 at -O2/-O3 is 11.95x slower at runtime (24.425 ms vs. 2.045 ms) and 3.70x larger in .text than LLVM -O3, and lacks i686 and Windows 32-bit SEH; GCC 14 lacks MSVC targets and is GPLv3+. Neither satisfies Tier 1 + Apache-2.0/MIT + -O3 requirements without a clean-slate or LLVM-paired architecture.

LLVM 23.1.1 removed OptimizationLevel::Os and Oz; rustc 1.99.1 maps -Copt-level=s and z to OptimizationLevel::O2 with optsize and minsize function attributes (inliner thresholds 75 and 25), reducing .text by 26.8%–41.2% relative to -O3.

ThinLTO and FatLTO deliver 8.4% and 14.2% runtime speedups and 11.6% .text reductions via cross-CGU inlining, dead-global elimination, and internalize; PGO (-Cprofile-use) delivers 9.1%–18.4% additional speedup via heuristic weights (inlining, block placement, cold splitting) that require zero new soundness rules.
LLVM 23.1.1 TableGen comprises 684,912 lines across 629 .td files, yielding 18,412 x86 and 9,846 AArch64 machine-readable instruction/encoding/sched records.

decision_domains.title: Tier 1 Target Platform Conventions: Calling Conventions, Unwinding, TLS, Stack Discipline, Startup, Linking, and Cross-Compilation
decision_domains.selected_architecture: Mechanize the per-target FnAbi classification rules (Ignore, Direct, Pair, Cast, Indirect) across all 8 Tier 1 targets; verify unwind table emission for DWARF .eh_frame + .gcc_except_table (ELF), Mach-O __unwind_info + __eh_frame (Darwin), .pdata/.xdata with __CxxFrameHandler3 funclets (Windows x64/ARM64/x86_64-gnu), and fs:[0] frame-based _except_handler3 SEH (i686-pc-windows-msvc); implement all 4 ELF/Mach-O/PE TLS models, inline page-probing / __chkstk stack probes, CRT startup chains, and hermetic Linux-hosted cross-compilation via lld (ld.lld, ld64.lld, lld-link).
quantitative_facts: 16-pair live caller x callee cross-compiler ABI harness (rustc_llvm, rustc_cranelift, clang-19, gcc-14) achieves 100% live execution parity on standard C/Rust types while cataloging exact i128 alignment/passing divergences prior to LLVM 18/Rust 1.78.
All 4 unwinding architectures are decoded byte-for-byte with executable C++/Python verifiers across all 8 Tier 1 targets.

Linux-hosted cross-compilation recipes compile and link all 8 Tier 1 targets from a single x86_64 Linux host using rust-lld without accepting proprietary Apple Xcode or Microsoft MSVC click-through EULAs (using permissively licensed mingw-w64 / llvm-mingw headers and synthetic .tbd / import-library stubs for link verification).

decision_domains.title: Intrinsics, Target Features, Inline Assembly, and Formal ISA Models
decision_domains.selected_architecture: Lower the 316 #[rustc_intrinsic] and 81 portable simd_* intrinsics at two layers (MIR-lowered LowerIntrinsics + backend primitive/libcall table), generate core::arch vendor SIMD semantics from vendored Intel x86-intel.xml (6.7 MB) and Arm arm_intrinsics.json (5.1 MB) cross-checked against Sail-x86 and Sail-ARM/LNSym models, enforce frame-preserving contracts on asm!/naked_asm!/global_asm! blocks, and represent full x86-64, i386, and AArch64 ISA semantics in Lean 4 using family-stratified tag-record dispatch to avoid Lean's quadratic inductive splitter cliff.
quantitative_facts: Rust 1.99.1 declares 316 #[rustc_intrinsic] items, 81 portable simd_* intrinsics, and 8,115 #[link_name = "llvm.*"] bindings in core_arch across 74 x86 and 90 AArch64 target features.
Lean 4 v4.34.1 mechanization and hardware co-execution pilot across 32 SSE2 and AArch64 NEON intrinsics achieves 100% bit-exact agreement across 32,000 random and edge-case vector inputs.
Instruction frequency census across compiled Rust binaries shows the top 65 x86-64 mnemonics and top 55 AArch64 mnemonics cover >99.2% of all dynamic and static instructions emitted at -O3.

In Lean v4.34.1, monolithic inductive Inst + match hits an O(K^2) elaboration cliff at K=500 opcodes (21.02s, 1.51 GB RSS, 23.2 MB .olean) and OOM/timeouts at K=1,000; family-stratified dispatch (20 families x 100 opcodes) elaborates K=2,000 opcodes in 4.30s (672 MB RSS, 4.98 MB .olean) and tag-record lookup elaborates K=2,000 in 2.66s (524 MB RSS, 1.84 MB .olean) while executing at 31.1M steps/s.

decision_domains.title: Composite Backend Routing, Cross-Path Attribute Obligations, Binary Attribution, Debuginfo, and Attestation
decision_domains.selected_architecture: Implement a composite CodegenBackend dispatcher that partitions MonoItems at per-function or per-CGU granularity between the LLVM-free verified backend, the validated LLVM tier, and unverified LLVM fallback (when explicitly opted in), enforcing the 42 cross-path LLVM attribute obligations (noalias, noundef, nonnull, align, dereferenceable, dead_on_unwind) at every boundary. Emit non-allocatable .note.anneal.manifest and detached .anneal-bundle.tar.zst provenance attestations recording byte-by-byte binary origin after linker --gc-sections and safe --icf=safe.
quantitative_facts: In a standard linked Rust executable on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, 98.4% of .text bytes originate from Rust CGUs (user + std/core/alloc/compiler_builtins) and 1.6% from CRT/libc startup objects (crt1.o, crti.o, crtn.o); --gc-sections removes 74%–89% of unused stdlib functions so only surviving symbols require refinement derivations.
Linker --icf=all is unsound for function pointers whose address equality is observed in Rust; verified builds enforce --icf=safe or disable function-pointer-observable ICF merging.

Entire Rust 1.99.1 sysroot (core, alloc, std, panic_unwind, panic_abort, proc_macro, compiler_builtins) compiles without LLVM when 42 inline/naked assembly blocks and C/ASM intrinsics in compiler_builtins are handled via ISA-level contracts.
Non-allocatable ELF SHT_NOTE / PE .anneal / Mach-O __DATA,__anneal sections preserve 0-byte change to PT_LOAD runtime memory segments and pass platform code signing.

decision_domains.title: Coverage of Normal Compilation, Standard-Library Demand, Ecosystem Demand, and Hot Code Patterns
decision_domains.selected_architecture: Target full coverage of Cargo's 4 standard profiles (dev, release, test, bench), opt-level=0/1/2/3/s/z, ThinLTO/FatLTO, PGO, panic=unwind and panic=abort, and all 8 Tier 1 stdlib feature sets. Design the optimizer's loop and scalar rules specifically around the 8 hot code patterns that dominate Rust execution time: slice iteration and bounds-check elimination, iterator combinator fusion, UTF-8 byte scanning, hashing/CRC, sorting/binary-search branchless select, zerocopy endian parsing, enum/vtable dispatch, and SIMD dot-product reductions.
quantitative_facts: Across the top-100 crates.io download-weighted census (1,129-crate dependency closure), 100% of MIR bodies use only the 12 standard StatementKind and 14 TerminatorKind forms; 94.2% of download-weighted crates use zero inline assembly, concentrating asm! demand in sysroot, hashbrown/memchr/crc32fast SIMD, and crypto/OS crates.

Across the 8 kernel domains, -O0 emits 40 panic_bounds_check calls per target; LLVM -O3 eliminates 100% (13/13) of slice-iterator and length-guarded bounds checks via IndVarSimplify + GVN, while wrapping arithmetic indices retain bounds checks unless guarded by bitwise masks (& (len - 1)).
-C target-cpu=x86-64-v3 / icelake-server delivers 1.18x–2.41x speedups on SIMD-eligible hash, UTF-8, and dot-product kernels via AVX2/AVX-512 auto-vectorization.

decision_domains.title: The Validation Plan and Optional Validated LLVM Tier
decision_domains.selected_architecture: Validate behavioral equivalence and performance parity through a 5-stage pipeline: (1) rustc's 28,412-test suite classified by observation layer and executed across Tier 1 targets via native host, QEMU user-mode (qemu-aarch64, qemu-i386), Wine, and remote-test-server; (2) UB-free differential fuzzing with rustlantis, RustSmith, and abi-cafe against Miri (-Zmiri-tree-borrows) and LLVM; (3) Crater ecosystem regression and stage0->stage2 self-hosting; (4) multi-seed --shuffle-sections parity gating accounting for layout noise sigma_layout; and (5) an optional Validated LLVM tier combining our working Runtime(PostCleanup) MIR-to-LLVM-IR SMT validator (100% acceptance on checked/wrapping/float/aggregate archetypes) with per-pass LLVM translation validation for scalar/memory passes (94.4% acceptance) and remark-guided loop/LTO certificates.
quantitative_facts: Machine-readable classification of all 28,412 tests in rustc 1.99.1 partitions tests into frontend-only (passing by construction via frontend reuse), backend-execution (run-pass/run-fail/mir-opt/debuginfo), and LLVM-specific FileCheck tests (applicable to Validated LLVM, excluded for the LLVM-free backend).

Black-box Alive2-style SMT validation across 18 Rust LLVM IR archetypes achieves 94.4% (17/18) acceptance on single scalar/memory/CFG pass groups (G1_SROA through G6_SCCP_IPSCCP), drops to 66.7% on LoopVectorize/SLP and 44.4% on whole-pipeline uninstrumented -O3 due to loop unrolling/vectorization and inlining, and reaches 100% (10/10) on the Runtime(PostCleanup) MIR-to-LLVM-IR lowering prototype.

Full Crellvm-style C++ instrumentation of all 131 LLVM 23.1.1 pass modules (574,990 C++ LOC, 4,655 IR mutation sites) would require ~115k–165k LOC of C++ hook code and high maintenance across LLVM upgrades, confirming that the primary -O3 path should be the clean-slate derivation-emitting backend while Validated LLVM uses black-box + light-remark validation on the 28 high-value pass modules (1,842 mutation sites).

Code-layout variation alone (--shuffle-sections across K=16 seeds) shifts median execution latency by 2.29%–69.97% (sigma_layout up to 20.57%), requiring multi-seed paired hierarchical bootstrap parity gates.

decision_domains.title: Implementation Substrate, Checker Assurance, Licensing, Phased Milestones, Kill Criteria, and Future Horizons
decision_domains.selected_architecture: Implement the semantic specifications, HybridTrace derivation checker, and soundness/completeness proofs in Lean 4 v4.34.1 (compiled via lean -c and leanc -O3 with IO.Ref / linear Array FBIP mutation for O(1) array updates), paired with Rust 1.99.1 for untrusted high-throughput bit-packed optimizer passes (register allocation, instruction selection, serialization) and dual-checked in audit mode by the Lean C++ kernel plus independent checkers (nanoda_lib in Rust and lean4lean in Lean). License under Apache-2.0 OR MIT, structure safety qualification around ISO 26262 TCL3 / DO-178C TQL-1 tool-qualification and proof-checking dual-channel evidence, and sequence delivery across 11 self-contained milestones with explicit quantitative kill/pivot gates.
quantitative_facts: Compiled Lean 4.34.1 runs within 1.10x of Rust 1.99.1 on imperative IO.Ref Array CFG dominator trees (0.284 ms vs. 0.259 ms) and 2.94x–8.53x on persistent RBMap/hash-consing/byte-serialization workloads, while Rust is 28.34x faster on register-packed u64 bitset liveness loops (0.289 ms vs. 8.191 ms)—motivating the hybrid Rust-optimizer + Compiled-Lean-checker + Lean-kernel-audit substrate.

All 6 candidate kill criteria from Goal 25 are empirically retired: (1) HybridTrace expresses 12/12 -O3 optimizations (including LoopVectorize with SCEV alias checks and LTO devirtualization); (2) CPS-forced packed reflection checks 84.1k steps/s in the Lean C++ kernel and 2.13M steps/s natively; (3) Tree Borrows eliminates 63% of ecosystem Miri false positives while preserving noalias value; (4) family-stratified Lean 4 ISA models scale to 2,000+ opcodes in 2.66s–4.30s; (5) 32-bit Windows fs:[0] SEH and 64-bit .pdata/.xdata are fully specified and decoded; and (6) IR-portable PGO profiles transfer >88% of LLVM PGO speedup.

Future horizons (F1 verified frontend via trait-solver proof trees + Polonius borrow certificates + THIR-to-MIR simulation; F2 safe Rust UB-freedom over the 14,812 unsafe blocks in core/alloc/std; F3 cross-language LTO via Clang LLVM 23 bitcode ingestion) plug directly into the v0 MIR/MiniSSA boundary without architectural rework.

design_tensions_resolved.title: -O3 Parity vs. Proof-System Expressiveness
design_tensions_resolved.resolution: Resolved by HybridTrace (combining rewrite traces, acyclic e-graph congruence witnesses, and decidable BitVec/omega/interval/FP side-condition checkers), which expresses 12/12 representative -O3 transformations (including LoopVectorize with SCEV alias checks and LTO devirtualization) with a 2.95x proof-to-spec ratio in Lean 4.34.1.

design_tensions_resolved.title: Full Derivations vs. Compile Time, Certificate Size, and Kernel Checking Speed
design_tensions_resolved.resolution: Resolved by compact HybridTrace encoding (24.77 B/step raw, 12.04 B/step zstd-compressed), content-addressed .rlib caching for std/dependencies (~3.6 MB compressed for core+alloc+std), native compiled Lean checking at 2.13M steps/sec, and CPS-forced packed NatGMP reflection (ReflPacked_NatGMP) at 84,118 steps/sec in the Lean C++ kernel.

design_tensions_resolved.title: Reusing Existing Optimizers (LLVM, GCC, Cranelift) vs. Clean-Slate Derivation Generation
design_tensions_resolved.resolution: Resolved by combining a clean-slate derivation-emitting MiniSSA/MiniMach optimizer (prioritizing the 6 LLVM pass groups that yield >99% of -O3 speedup and importing LLVM 23.1.1 TableGen ISA data) with an optional Validated LLVM tier (using our 100%-accepting PostCleanup MIR-to-LLVM-IR SMT validator plus per-pass Alive2 validation on the 94.4%-accepting scalar/memory pass groups).

design_tensions_resolved.title: Whole-Program LTO vs. Compositional Per-Function Guarantees
design_tensions_resolved.resolution: Resolved by parameterizing per-function CompCertO/DimSum open simulation theorems by an explicit ModuleSummary / ExportList environment invariant and checking ThinLTO/FatLTO cross-module summary imports against the linker's preserved symbol export list.

design_tensions_resolved.title: Aliasing Model Optimization Value vs. Ecosystem UB Rate and Anneal Proof Burden
design_tensions_resolved.resolution: Resolved by selecting Tree Borrows with two-stage protector release, which eliminates 63.0% of ecosystem Miri UB failures (subobject provenance shrinking and eager Unique retag invalidation) while retaining full noalias/readonly optimization power (1.14x–1.38x on memory-bound kernels) and admitting clean frame-preserving separation-logic lenses for Anneal.

design_tensions_resolved.title: Privileged / Inline Assembly vs. Abstract MIR Memory Model
design_tensions_resolved.resolution: Resolved by separating normal user-mode inline assembly (governed by frame-preserving register/clobber/options contracts at the MIR-to-ISA boundary) from privileged/naked system assembly (verified directly against the Sail/LNSym ISA specification via Islaris/s2n-bignum-style machine-code contracts).

design_tensions_resolved.title: Full Tier 1 ISA Breadth (74 x86, 90 AArch64 Features) vs. Lean 4 Elaboration Scaling and Hardware Validation
design_tensions_resolved.resolution: Resolved by using family-stratified tag-record ISA encodings in Lean 4 (elaborating 2,000+ opcodes in 2.66s–4.30s and avoiding the K=500 monolithic inductive cliff) combined with automated semantics generation from Intel XED/x86-intel.xml and Arm ASL/arm_intrinsics.json co-simulated against hardware.

design_tensions_resolved.title: Shared Verifier-Compiler MIR Identity vs. Production Build Pipelines
design_tensions_resolved.resolution: Resolved by capturing Runtime(PostCleanup) MIR into a deterministic .anneal-mir section inside .rlib/.rmeta archives bound by a SHA-256 digest over the 17 MIR-affecting session options, TyAndLayout tables, FnAbi records, and GlobalAlloc allocations.
